learning_outcomes.text: Acquire fundamental concepts of Classical Physics and the basic physical principles and knowledge preparatory for subsequent years' courses, specifically concepts of force, work, energy, fundamental interaction fields, and the correct problem-solving methodology.

Develop awareness and mastery of physical phenomena related to classical mechanics and electromagnetism, enabling autonomous identification and use of the appropriate descriptive physical model to characterize a given problem and/or identify characteristics and requirements that measuring instruments must satisfy.

Demonstrate acquisition of the physical investigation method, based on the analysis of experimental evidence and the consequent formulation of hypotheses that guide the construction of a descriptive model.

Recognize the characteristics and dynamics of a given physical problem, in order to trigger a sequence of logical reasoning that allows reaching a solution by adapting the studied approaches and resolution strategies.

syllabus_topics: Physics measurements: Physical quantities, standards and units of measurement. Precision and significant figures. Dimensional analysis.

Kinematics of a material point: Elements of vector calculus. One-dimensional motion: time equation, average and instantaneous velocity and acceleration. Concept of trajectory, curvilinear abscissa, center and radius of curvature. Motion in space: position, velocity and acceleration vectors and their Cartesian, polar, tangential and normal components to the trajectory. Planar motion in Cartesian coordinates: motion of projectiles. Circular motion: vectorial relationships between r, v, a and w, a.

Dynamics of a material point: Fundamental interactions. Principle of inertia and introduction to the concept of force. Newton's laws. Inertial reference frames. Momentum and impulse. Examples of forces: weight, elastic, static and dynamic friction, constraint reactions, tensions. Simple pendulum. Kinetic energy, Work, Power. Work and change in kinetic energy. Conservative forces. Potential energy and conservation of mechanical energy. Work of non-conservative forces and principle of energy conservation. Analysis of potential energy diagrams. Angular momentum. Torque. Angular momentum theorem. Relative motions (brief notes): reference frames in relative translational, rotational motion. Theorem of relative velocities. Non-inertial reference frames. Apparent forces. Galilean relativity principle.

Dynamics of systems of material points: External and internal forces. Center of mass. I and II cardinal equations of motion. Conservation of momentum and angular momentum. Equilibrium conditions. Properties of the center of mass. CM system. König's theorems. Work and kinetic energy. Potential energy.

Rigid body dynamics: Center of gravity. Systems of parallel forces. Definition and properties of rigid bodies. Mass density, position of the center of mass. Motion of a rigid body. Rigid body rotating about a fixed axis: kinetic energy, angular momentum and moment of inertia. Huygens-Steiner theorem. Compound pendulum. Instantaneous axis of rotation. Angular impulse and impulse moment. Pure rolling motion. Free rigid body. Cardinal equations of motion. Static equilibrium of the rigid body.

Collisions and oscillations: Impulsive forces. Collisions in isolated/non-isolated systems. Elastic and inelastic collisions. Application to two-particle systems. Central collisions. Collisions between material points and rigid bodies. Collisions with free/constrained rigid bodies. Oscillations: Differential equation of the harmonic oscillator and its properties. Energy of the harmonic oscillator. Central force fields (brief notes): Properties and conservation laws. Gravitational force. Kepler's laws. Inertial and gravitational mass. Law of universal gravitation. Gravitational field and potential. Motion of a body subject to gravitational force.

Electrostatic force and electrostatic field: Electric charge. Electrical structure of matter. Coulomb's force. Electrostatic field. Electrostatic field lines. Motion of a charge in an electrostatic field. Systems of point charges. Millikan's experiment.

Electric work and electrostatic potential: Work of electric force: definition of voltage and potential difference. Electrostatic potential. Electrostatic potential energy. The field as a potential gradient. Equipotential surfaces. Electric dipole and force on an electric dipole.
Gauss's Law: Flux of the electrostatic field. Gauss's theorem in integral form. Applications and consequences of Gauss's theorem.

Conductors and dielectrics: Conducting bodies in electrostatic equilibrium. Hollow conductor and electrostatic screen. Capacitance of isolated conductors. Complete induction between 2 conductors: capacitors. Systems of capacitors in series and parallel. Energy of the electrostatic field. Dielectrics. Dielectric constant. Polarization. General equations of electrostatics in the presence of dielectrics.

Electric current: Electric conduction. Electric current and stationary electric current. Current density j. Ohm's law and concept of electrical resistance. Electrical power and Joule effect. Classical model of electrical conduction. Electromotive forces. Resistor systems in series and parallel. Displacement current. Brief note on Kirchhoff's laws for electrical networks.

Magnetostatics: Magnetic field and magnetic force: Magnetic interaction. Magnetic field. Correlations between electricity and magnetism. Magnetic force on a moving charge. Magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor. Mechanical magnetic moments on planar circuits. Hall effect. Motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field with calculation examples. Sources of the magnetic field and Ampere's law: magnetic field produced by a current. Calculations of magnetic fields produced by particular circuits. Electrodynamic actions between current-carrying wires. Ampere's law.

Time-varying electric and magnetic fields: Faraday's law and electromagnetic induction. Origin of the magnetic field and induced EMF. Applications of Faraday's law. Self-induction. Magnetic energy. Mutual induction. Ampere-Maxwell's law. Maxwell's equations (brief notes).
teaching_methods: Notes in electronic format (.pdf) provided by the lecturer for in-depth topics

assessment_methods.method: Written test for Module A (3 theoretical questions, 3 numerical exercises)
Written test for Module B (3 theoretical questions, 3 numerical exercises)

assessment_rules: The assessment covers all program topics and requires knowledge of the topics and the ability to apply the tools and techniques discussed, demonstrating mastery of vocabulary and technical terminology. It consists of two tests, one for Module A and one for Module B, normally written and lasting 75 minutes each. Each module test verifies theoretical concepts (3 questions per module) and application skills (3 exercises per module). The minimum condition to pass each module is an overall score of at least 18/30, resulting from correctly solving two out of three exercises and answering at least one theoretical question exhaustively. The final grade for General Physics will be the average of the individual grades obtained for the two modules. Students demonstrating the ability to apply knowledge and skills in contexts beyond those presented in class will be awarded cum laude.
